audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Lucian Levels 1 through 5 and called 6 onward 'Skill', on a 35.14% lane over 37 games — and against its own whys, which say the lane flips at 3 ('it's a coin-flip'), that 4-5 is his drain window, and that he 'out-scales hard'.
audit.why: The packet chart (Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Sylas, Sylas, Sylas, Sylas) matches the prose exactly. Levels 1-2 are Lucian's before Kingslayer can heal a trade back; from 3 Chain Lash's 775 range and the Abscond recast contest the kite; from 4 the heal wins the attrition.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Lucian / Lucian / Skill / Sylas / Sylas / Sylas / Sylas in both layers; diff EVEN -> HARD with matching tone, ratings and difficulty prose.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Lvl 2-3 Lucian window, Lvl 6 Hijack stealing The Culling, Lvl 3-6 the E1-E2 catch, 2+ items scaling. All four are Sylas-owned or Lucian-owned in the right order against the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chain Lash appears nowhere on this page and neither does its range or its second hit.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sylas lashes his chains out, intersecting at his targeted location dealing damage to and slowing enemies. After a delay, magical energy explodes from the intersection point dealing damage.' 775 range on 10/9/8/7/6s against Piercing Light's 500 means he out-ranges your poke outright, and the delayed second hit at the intersection means walking through the crossing point after the first tick still costs you. That is the whole reason Level 3 stops being yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer describes his E only as 'Dash into chain-stun', with no numbers and no mention of what the recast actually does.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' The recast pulls HIM to YOU — so backing off to 500 units after he dashes does not put you out of reach, which is exactly the mistake a Lucian makes holding Relentless Pursuit. 13/12/11/10/9s, 400 range per cast.
audit.corrected: Two-part mechanic and cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' but never says which ability or when 'early' is.
audit.why: Kingslayer is the heal — 400 range, 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s, 'dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions'. It reaches a 6s cooldown at rank 5, which is why extended trades stop going your way at 4-5. The flagged missing interaction for this matchup is exactly this.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now names Kingslayer and puts the Executioner's timing before his first item.

edits.after: Chain Lash reaches 775 to your 500, and the Abscond recast pulls him onto you — the kite is contested now.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Abscond / Abduct — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Kingslayer heals him through your poke and falls toward a 6s cooldown by rank 5 — his sustain out-lasts your chip.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Hijack steals The Culling at 950 range — never channel your ult where he can take it and fire it back.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: His first AP item makes Kingslayer out-trade you outright, and Chain Lash's slow shuts off the kite you rely on.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: A two-item Sylas heals through your DPS and bursts your frame — defer to your team and stop hunting the duel.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Abscond is 13s at rank 1 and only 400 range — punish him hard the moment he spends it.

edits.after: Kingslayer heals him off you — buy Executioner's before his first item, not after.

notes: Both layers currently call Abduct a stun ('chain-stun', 'his E2 stun'). Riot's own text in the kit file says only 'throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — it does not mention a stun, and the E carries no hardCC flag. I did not assert a stun anywhere new, and I did not delete the existing claims either, since removing a true mechanic would be worse than leaving it; recorded in unverified for someone with the live tooltip to settle. Hijack is 80/55/30s — by rank 3 it is up almost every fight, which makes 'hold The Culling until his R is down' much weaker advice late than the content layer implies; I left wants.you[2] alone rather than rewrite it on an assumption.
